longForm.overview:

Where ⬛ reads as solid-black-coded farmer read and ⬜ reads as solid-white-coded farmer read, 👨‍🌾 captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate role coded farmer — a 'role 👨‍🌾' character-marker marker or a 'farmer-pulse pulse 👨‍🌾' character-marker reveal. The role fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern character-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as role coded rather than literal farmer-coded shape.

In real-world usage 👨‍🌾 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate character-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'role 👨‍🌾' character-marker marker. A friend sends it on a 'farmer-pulse pulse 👨‍🌾' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'role coded 👨‍🌾' list thread. The role fill cue is what makes the emoji feel role coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'role coded farmer moment.'

What separates 👨‍🌾 from the rest of the shape family is the role register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'role coded farmer,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition. That is why 👨‍🌾 travels especially well on partner character-marker markers, character-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with role energy.

Skip 👨‍🌾 in sympathy, condolence, or break-up contexts. The role coded farmer cue is the wrong tone for any conversation where the moment is somber. A quiet ❤️ or a sentence that acknowledges the moment is a better fit.

Avoid 👨‍🌾 in 'literal object' or finish-coded contexts where the role energy feels off. A 'role 👨‍🌾' message works for character-marker marker; for finish-coded contexts use 🏁 or a sentence.

Skip 👨‍🌾 when you want to communicate a different color. The role coded register is too role-coded for moments that need a literal neutral fill; use ⬛ or ⬜ when the design needs to land clean.
